main_body: A tall three-storey brick shopfront with a slate mansard roof, two dormers, a chimney, a balcony and a striped-awning shop window, all seen straight on.
top_band: Rows 17-23 at x=32: a grey-blue band (L=122 edge, then L=95 for 5 rows, then L=122). It is a flat panel on the roof, in the same lightness family as the slate below (L 79-103), not a separate lighter top surface.
evidence: The whole building is a vertical facade. The scan shows rows 17-23 at L 95-122 flowing into the slate at L 79-103, so there is no step of 25 L or more to a distinct top surface. The roof reads as a vertical mansard face with a flat panel above it, not a sloped roof seen from above. The walls, windows, balcony and awning are all face-on vertical surfaces. The reference houses show large sloped roof planes seen from above, which this drawing lacks. The window insets are minor and do not rescue the projection.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and glowing windows carry several tones and good texture, and the median of 14 colours per tile sits between the two references (18 and 11). Flat-fill coverage is only 2%. However, 91% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7-9% in the references, so the outlines are a neutral dark line rather than a darker version of the adjacent material. Distinct colours total 56, far below the 185 and 66 of the references. Together these give a thinner, more sticker-like look than the Beodeul pieces.
